name: Trazodone
summary: An atypical antidepressant (SARI) that today is used far more often at low doses as a hypnotic than at full antidepressant doses.
mechanism: Antagonizes 5-HT2A receptors and weakly inhibits serotonin reuptake; strong H1 and α1-adrenergic antagonism drives sedation and hypotension.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Sedation within 1 h; antidepressant effect 2–6 weeks

dosing.adult: Insomnia (off-label): 25–100 mg at bedtime; depression: 150 mg/day in divided doses, up to 400 mg/day

safety.lactation: Limited data; present in breast milk.
warnings: Priapism — rare but urgent; emergency care needed
safety.overdose: Sedation, hypotension, and QT prolongation; priapism possible — supportive care.

clinicalPearls: At 25–100 mg it behaves mainly as a hypnotic; antidepressant doses are 150 mg and above.
Strong CYP3A4 substrate — potent CYP3A4 inhibitors can spike levels.
good: Insomnia (especially in depression) and depression where sedation is desirable.
bad: Men (priapism risk), orthostatic hypotension, or concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
